ukmt-jmo-2026-01.title: Write as 11x+S
ukmt-jmo-2026-01.body: Let $x=\overline{YUM}$. Then $\overline{YUMS}=10x+S$ and the sum is $11x+S=2026$. $2026=11\times184+2$, so $x=184$, $S=2$. If $x$ changed by $1$, $S$ would change by $11$, impossible for a digit. So $Y=1,U=8,M=4,S=2$ is the unique solution. ∎

ukmt-jmo-2026-02.title: Divisibility by 3
ukmt-jmo-2026-02.body: Among $m,m+1,m+2$ one is a multiple of $3$, so the product is divisible by $3$. Let $n=\frac{m(m+1)(m+2)}3$, an integer. The product is at least $6$, so $n\ge2$ and $n-1>0$. Then $(n-1)+n+(n+1)=3n=m(m+1)(m+2)$. ∎

ukmt-jmo-2026-03.title: Track the piles
ukmt-jmo-2026-03.body: Start with $(L,R)$ for Blackbeard, Brownbeard. After night 1: $(L+3,R-3)\to\left(\frac{L+3}2,\frac{L+2R-3}2\right)$ (Brownbeard adds half of $L+3$ to $R-3$). Night 2: Brownbeard takes $3$: $\left(\frac{L-3}2,\frac{L+2R+3}2\right)$, then Blackbeard takes half of Brownbeard's: Brownbeard has $\frac{L+2R+3}4$. This equals $R$, so $L+2R+3=4R$, i.e. $L+R=3R-3=3(R-1)$. ∎

ukmt-jmo-2026-04.title: Complementary counting
ukmt-jmo-2026-04.body:
Total choices $\binom83=56$. A face has $4$ vertices, so $4$ triples; $6$ faces give $24$ (no triple lies on two faces). $56-24=32$.

**Answer: 32**

ukmt-jmo-2026-04.title: Classify
ukmt-jmo-2026-04.body:
Triples containing an antipodal pair: $4$ pairs $\times6$ third vertices $=24$, none on a common face. Without an antipodal pair and not on a face: three of the four vertices of one colour class of the cube: $4+4=8$. Total $32$.

**Answer: 32**

ukmt-jmo-2026-05.title: Angles at F
ukmt-jmo-2026-05.body: $\angle AFE=120^\circ$ and $FE$ is a diagonal of square $EIFJ$, so $\angle EFJ=45^\circ$ and $\angle AFJ=75^\circ$. In square $ABGH$ with $\angle FAB=120^\circ$, $\angle FAH=30^\circ$, and $AF=AH$ (equal sides), so $\angle AFH=\frac{180-30}2=75^\circ$. Thus $\angle AFH=\angle AFJ$ and $H$ lies on $FJ$. ∎

ukmt-jmo-2026-06.title: Colour the board
ukmt-jmo-2026-06.body:
Colour the grid like a chessboard (centre and corners white, edge-middles black). Moves alternate colours, so the path is: first move to a black square ($4$ choices), then $n-1$ two-step moves black $\to$ white $\to$ black, then a forced final move to the centre. From a black square: $2$ moves to a corner (then $2$ ways back to black) and $1$ to the centre (then $4$ ways): $2\cdot2+4=8$ ways. Total $4\cdot8^{n-1}=2^{3n-1}$. (Check: $n=1$: $4$.)

**Answer: $4\cdot8^{n-1}$**
